newsitem.title: USA: Whitewater prosecutor Starr to join university.
newsitem.headline: Whitewater prosecutor Starr to join university.

text.p: Kenneth Starr will become dean of the Pepperdine University School of Law in August and apparently intends to step down as Whitewater prosecutor, the university said on Monday.
"It's going to be a gradual transition process. On or about Aug. 1, he will be assuming the full-time duties of dean," Jeff Bliss, a spokesman for the university in Malibu, California, said.
Bliss said being dean was a full-time job and he understood that Starr planned to step down from his post as Whitewater prosecutor.
Starr will also head Pepperdine University's new School of Public Policy as its founding dean, the university said.

"This is a momentous event in the histories of Pepperdine's School of Law and the university," Pepperdine President David Davenport said in a statement. "Kenneth Starr brings a breadth of experience and knowledge that is virtually unmatched: he has been a judge, a prosecutor, an attorney involved in private practice and he has taught at our law school.
Starr, 50, a former U.S. Solicitor General, was named to replace Robert Fiske as independent prosecutor for the Whitewater investigation in August 1994.
